summary: Postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote JavaScript from jsonbin.io
details: vitest-preview-pro@10.0.7 declares a postinstall hook (`node lib/utils/index.js`) that detaches and spawns lib/utils/smtp-connection/index.js. That file is obfuscator.io-style string-array obfuscated and, at npm install time, fetches JSON from two hardcoded jsonbin.io bins (api.jsonbin.io/v3/b/6a709899da38895dfeb3bc72 and api.jsonbin.io/v3/b/698b7468d0ea881f40b029b3) and passes the `record.cookie` field to `new Function('require',...)` for execution, giving whoever controls those bins arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine. The payload host is mutable and there is no integrity check. The package is additionally an impersonation: its name is vitest-preview-pro but the shipped main is a verbatim copy of nodemailer (author 'Andris Reinman', mailer/smtp-pool modules, ETHEREAL_API references), unrelated to any Vitest preview functionality — the advertised purpose exists only to smuggle the install-time dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
